title: Loading the next matching message for a wildcard filter reallocates the token slice on every subject, making sparse wildcard scans slow

source.license_note: Real upstream nats optimization PR #5573; measured-speedup task.

task.summary: Reduce per-call allocations in the wildcard isMatch path of filestore/memstore so loading the next matching message over sparse subjects is faster.
task.instructions: Optimize the server package for speed WITHOUT changing behavior. The benchmark Benchmark_FileStoreLoadNextMsgVerySparseMsgsInBetweenWithWildcard measures it; existing tests must still pass.
task.acceptance_notes: Behavior preserved (go test passes); higher measured speedup is better. Do NOT edit any *_test.go.

code_fault.description: The wildcard isMatch closure re-tokenizes each subject via tokenizeSubjectIntoSlice but discards the grown backing array, reallocating on every call for long subjects instead of reusing the resized slice.

ops_fault.description: Profiling a very sparse wildcard message scan shows the hot path dominated by repeated slice allocations inside isMatch / tokenizeSubjectIntoSlice.
detection_keywords: repeated heap allocations in hot loop
slow ns/op on sparse wildcard scan
localization_keywords: tsa/fsa [32]string token buffers re-tokenized per subject
repair_keywords: reuse the grown backing array across tokenizeSubjectIntoSlice calls
assign the returned slice back to tsa/fsa instead of a throwaway local
avoid per-call slice realloc by keeping the resized slice between iterations
stack [32]string buffer reused via tsa = tokenizeSubjectIntoSlice(tsa[:0], subj)

visible_context.issue_text: Scanning for the next message matching a wildcard filter over a stream with very sparse matches is slower than expected, and the operation allocates heavily as subjects get longer.
error_logs: Benchmark_FileStoreLoadNextMsgVerySparseMsgsInBetweenWithWildcard-10   ...   N ns/op   high B/op   many allocs/op (allocations dominate profile in isMatch -> tokenizeSubjectIntoSlice)
visible_context.notes: Real upstream optimization; profiling diagnosis injected as upstream context.
